title: Design a Social News Feed (Twitter / X Timeline)
subtitle: Hybrid fan-out (write vs read), celebrity skew mitigation & cursor pagination
functionalReqs: Users can publish posts containing text and optional image/video media.
Users load their Home Timeline sorted reverse-chronologically (or ranked) with <200ms p99 latency.

nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Instant scroll feel drives core user retention.
Eventual consistency is acceptable for social timelines.
Users should always see a feed even if recent second posts lag slightly.

workedSummary.feedReadsPerSec: ~10,000 QPS avg, ~30,000 QPS peak (assuming 5 timeline opens/day)
workedSummary.celebrityFanoutProblem: 1 post from a 50M-follower celebrity = 50M Redis pushes under naive write fan-out!

coreEntities.name: Post
coreEntities.storageEngine: Sharded Postgres / DynamoDB (partition by post_id or user_id)

coreEntities.name: FollowGraph
coreEntities.storageEngine: Sharded Graph/KV Store (partition by follower_id + reverse index)

apiContracts.purpose: Create post and trigger async hybrid fan-out
Fetch paginated home feed via monotonic Snowflake cursor

explorerTopology.title: Hybrid Fan-Out News Feed Architecture
explorerTopology.subtitle: Push normal posts to follower Redis ZSETs; merge celebrity posts at read time
explorerTopology.overview: Pure fan-out-on-write collapses when a celebrity with 50M followers posts; pure fan-out-on-read stalls when a user follows 2,000 accounts. Hybrid fan-out combines pre-materialized Redis timelines for normal authors with fast read-time merge of followed celebrities.
keyTakeaways: Store only `(post_id, timestamp)` inside Redis timeline ZSETs—hydrate post bodies in batch to save RAM.
Threshold (e.g., >10,000 followers) splits accounts into push-fan-out vs pull-on-read celebrities.
Use cursor-based pagination (`post_id < cursor`) instead of SQL `OFFSET` to avoid shifting duplicates on new posts.

nodes.label: Mobile App
nodes.summary: Publishes posts and scrolls paginated timeline.
failureModes: Duplicate post submission on flaky mobile network without clientRequestId

nodes.label: Timeline & Post Service
nodes.summary: Writes post to DB+Kafka on publish; merges precomputed ZSET + celebrity posts on read.
failureModes: N+1 hydration queries if posts aren't batch-fetched via MGET

nodes.label: Post Events (Kafka)
nodes.summary: Buffers new posts so publish API returns in <15ms before fan-out runs.
whenToUse: Decoupling post creation from follower fan-out
failureModes: Consumer lag delays follower visibility during viral events

nodes.label: Fan-Out Workers
nodes.summary: If author < 10k followers, pipelines ZADD into active followers' Redis timelines; otherwise skips push.
failureModes: Wasting RAM pushing to dormant accounts inactive for >30 days

nodes.label: Redis Timeline & Celeb Cache
nodes.summary: Holds top 800 `post_id` entries per active user + cached recent posts of celebrities.
failureModes: Cache eviction requires fallback rebuild from social graph

nodes.label: Post Store & Media CDN
nodes.summary: Stores canonical post text/metadata; images/videos reside in S3 behind CDN.
failureModes: Slow hydration if post cache misses hit disk

steps.info: Post persisted with Snowflake ID; PostCreated emitted -> User gets 201 Created
steps.inspectorNote: Author doesn't wait for fan-out—write path completes after DB insert + Kafka ack.

steps.info: Author has 420 (<10k) followers -> pipeline ZADD into active follower ZSETs
steps.inspectorNote: Dormant users (inactive >30 days) are skipped during fan-out and built lazily on login.

steps.info: Fetch top 20 IDs from user ZSET + top posts from 3 followed celebrities -> K-way merge
steps.inspectorNote: K-way merge in memory takes <1ms because each celebrity's recent post list is already cached in Redis.

steps.info: MGET post:1892... -> hydrate 20 posts -> return JSON + nextCursor
steps.payloadInspector: Batch hydrated 20 posts (16 from Post Cache, 4 from DB) in 5ms
steps.inspectorNote: Total feed read stays well under 50ms server-side.

chaosScenarios.title: Celebrity with 60M Followers Posts (Bypass Write Amplification)
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: A mega-celebrity (60M followers) tweets during a live global broadcast.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Hybrid check (`followers >= 10,000`) skips 60M Redis writes completely, writing once to `celeb_timeline:{id}` and merging on read.

steps.info: is_celebrity=true (60M followers) -> SKIP 60M fan-out; write 1 entry to celeb_posts:999
steps.inspectorNote: Prevents fan-out queues from backing up for all normal users.

steps.info: Readers merge celeb_posts:999 from read-replicated/local-L1 cache
steps.payloadInspector: Local pod L1 cache (TTL 5s) absorbs hot celeb_posts:999 reads!
steps.inspectorNote: Adding a 5-second in-process L1 cache on celebrity post lists prevents single-shard Redis hot-key overload.

pros: Protects Redis/workers from mega-celebrity write storms
cons: Slightly more complex read-path K-way merge & dynamic threshold tuning
tradeoffs.bestFor: Twitter/X, Instagram, LinkedIn feeds with skewed follower graphs

cons: Fails catastrophically on celebrity posts (minutes of lag + massive RAM bloat)
tradeoffs.bestFor: Symmetric capped friend graphs (e.g. Facebook max 5,000 friends)

deepDives.title: Celebrity Hot-Key on Read Merge
deepDives.bottleneck: If 2M followers open their feed simultaneously after a celebrity posts, `celeb_posts:999` hammers one Redis shard.
deepDives.solution: Add a short 5-second local in-memory cache on Timeline Service pods (or replicate celebrity ZSET across N read replicas).
deepDives.tradeoff: Up to 5s propagation delay for celebrity tweets in exchange for 100x lower Redis shard pressure.

deepDives.title: Offset vs Cursor Pagination
deepDives.bottleneck: `OFFSET 20` shifts items downward whenever new posts arrive, showing duplicate posts on page 2.
deepDives.solution: Pass monotonic Snowflake `cursor = last_seen_post_id` and query `score < cursor`.
deepDives.tradeoff: Users cannot jump directly to 'Page 47'—ideal for infinite scroll feeds.

criteria: Distinguishes read-heavy feed vs write path
Stores lightweight post_ids in Redis ZSETs + hydrates bodies
Explains write vs read fan-out trade-off
Uses Kafka to keep publish fast
Adds local L1 cache for hot celebrity keys
